evidence.note: First boto3 403 treated as signal about the auth design: agent diagnoses body-consumption in middleware and revises architecture to two-phase auth (tenant-resolve vs full-verify) — genuine design revision, not a symptom patch.
Recognizes the two-phase design forces a double body read and pivots again to a single verify_signature using x-amz-content-sha256 — a second decisive design pivot on the signing model.
Root-cause diagnosis: missing unquote import raising a NameError swallowed by a blanket except, causing anonymous fallback and the 403 — correct causal reasoning about the signing failure.

Terminal enters a stuck state; agent repeats the same ineffective recovery moves (Ctrl-C/Ctrl-D/heredoc terminators) for ~120 steps without adapting approach — failure to course-correct on a diverged reality.
Never manages to re-run the boto3 test to confirm the auth design fixes worked; ends with repeated 'Mark task complete' submits — the re-verification loop for the design corrections never closes.

reasoning: Early on the agent clearly treats signing/auth verification failures as signal about the design, revising the auth architecture twice and diagnosing real root causes — anchor-8-level behavior on the core signing example. But that quality is not sustained: once the terminal diverges, it flails on the same ineffective recovery for ~150 steps and never re-verifies that its design fixes actually resolved the 403, so the 'propagate and confirm with targeted re-verification' half of the high anchors is absent. Netting strong early design revision against the collapsed re-verification and long non-adaptive stretch places it at the 5 level (diagnoses actual causes and revises design choices when checks fail, but without closing the loop).
